name: Ibn Abbas
title: Interpreter of the Quran (Turjuman al-Quran)
biography: The paternal cousin of Prophet Muhammad, universally revered in Sunni tradition as the 'Ink of the Community' (Hibr al-Ummah) and 'Interpreter of the Quran' (Turjuman al-Quran). Having studied recitation directly under Ubayy bin Ka'b and Zaid bin Thabit, Ibn Abbas maintained a personal codex and oral recitation tradition in Mecca that frequently diverged from the Uthmanic text. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, and Tafsir al-Tabari, he repeatedly defends non-Uthmanic readings—such as 'in front of them was a king seizing every sound ship' (18:79), 'in the seasons of Hajj' (2:198), and attributes several Uthmanic consonantal forms (such as tasta'nisu in 24:27 and qada in 17:23) to scribal slips.

virtues.hadith_arabic: ضَمَّنِي النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى صَدْرِهِ وَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ عَلِّمْهُ الْحِكْمَةَ
virtues.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn Abbas: Once the Prophet (ﷺ) embraced me and said: "O Allah! Bestow on him the knowledge of the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom."

variants.short_title: Added Negation 'Not to Go Around' in Surah 2:158
variants.plain_english_hook: The codices of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas included the word 'not' in Surah 2:158 ('no blame if he does not go around Safa and Marwa'), reversing the verse into an exemption from the ritual.
variants.title: Addition of the Negative Particle 'La' ('An La Yattawwafa Bihima') in Surah 2:158
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'fa-lā junāḥa 'alayhi an yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' ('there is no blame on him if he goes around both of them'), Tafsir al-Tabari (#1953–1954) documents that the codex of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the recitation of Ibn Abbas included the negative particle 'lā' ('an lā yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' — 'there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them'). Based on this codex reading, early jurists such as Ata', Anas bin Malik, and Ibn Sirin ruled that walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah is optional, whereas Aisha (in Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495) rejected that legal conclusion by appealing to the Uthmanic wording without 'lā'.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
variants.uthmanic_target_english: (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
variants.variant_target_english: (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
variants.variant_full_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495, Aisha defends the Uthmanic reading by explaining the historical occasion of revelation (the Ansar's pre-Islamic hesitation to walk between the two hills), while al-Tabari argues that even if 'lā' was written in Ibn Mas'ud's codex, it could be interpreted as a pleonastic (redundant) negation.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit transmission (#1953–1954) that Ata' and other early authorities derived the non-obligatory status of Sa'i directly 'because of the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them' proves that the particle 'lā' was understood by its readers as a substantive legal negation, not a grammatical redundancy.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 1953 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار , قال : ثنا أبو عاصم , قال : ثنا ابن جريج , قال : قال عطاء : لو أن حاجا أفاض بعدما رمى جمرة العقبة فطاف بالبيت ولم يسع , فأصابها - يعني امرأته - لم يكن عليه شيء , لا حج ولا عمرة ; من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما " ... 1954 - حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم , قال : ثنا هشيم , قال : أخبرنا عبد الملك , عن عطاء , عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : { إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله } الآية , { فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما } .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 1953 - Muhammad b. Bashshar narrated to us, from Abu 'Asim, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said: If a pilgrim departs after he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and went around the House and did not hasten, then touched her—meaning his wife—there would be nothing upon him, not in Hajj nor in 'Umrah; due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them." ... 1954 - Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to me, from Hushaym, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: {Surely al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God}, the verse, "(there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Reads 'Those Who Can Barely Bear It' (2:184)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran says 'for those who can afford it' there is a ransom of feeding a poor person instead of fasting. Ibn Abbas and Aisha read 'for those who are burdened by it'—reversing who qualifies.
variants.title: Passive 'Yutawwaqunahu' vs. Active 'Yutiqunahu' in Q. 2:184 (Ibn Abbas & Aisha)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4505 and Tafsir al-Tabari (which also records the same reading from Aisha), Ibn 'Abbas recited Q. 2:184 with a consonantal and morphological shift as 'وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ' (passive *yuṭawwaqūnahu*, with a doubled *wāw*: 'for those who are heavily burdened with it / can barely bear it') rather than the Uthmanic 'وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ' (active *yuṭīqūnahu*, with a *yā'*: 'for those who can afford it'). Under the Uthmanic wording, healthy believers could initially pay a ransom instead of fasting, forcing jurists to declare the verse abrogated by Q. 2:185; under Ibn 'Abbas's reading, the verse was never abrogated and permanently applies to the elderly who can barely endure fasting.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: And for those who can afford it,
variants.variant_target_english: And for those who are heavily burdened with it,
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةٞ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينٖۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew.
variants.variant_full_arabic: أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ فِدۡيَةٞ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينٖۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who are heavily burdened with it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari rejects Ibn 'Abbas's reading because it alters the consonantal skeleton (rasm) of the Uthmanic Mushafs (replacing ya' with waw), arguing instead that the Uthmanic wording was revealed first and subsequently abrogated by Q. 2:185.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4505, Ibn 'Abbas explicitly denies that Q. 2:184 was ever abrogated ('laysat bi-mansukhah') and bases the permanent legal ruling for elderly men and women directly on his non-Uthmanic reading 'yutawwaqunahu,' which al-Tabari admits was also recited by Aisha.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ata' from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْحَاقُ، أَخْبَرَنَا رَوْحٌ، حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ لَيْسَتْ بِمَنْسُوخَةٍ، هُوَ الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ الْكَبِيرَةُ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعَانِ أَنْ يَصُومَا، فَلْيُطْعِمَانِ مَكَانَ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مِسْكِينًا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated 'Ata': One heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting: 'And for those who are heavily burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person...' (2:184). Ibn 'Abbas said, 'This Verse is not abrogated, but it is meant for a very old man and a very old woman who have no strength to fast, so they should feed a poor person for every day in place of fasting.'
hadiths.highlight_arabic: سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ لَيْسَتْ بِمَنْسُوخَةٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: One heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting: 'And for those who are heavily burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person...'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما قوله : { وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين } فإن قراءة كافة المسلمين : { وعلى الذين يطيقونه } وعلى ذلك خطوط مصاحفهم ... وكان ابن عباس يقرؤها فيما روي عنه : " وعلى الذين يطوقونه " ... 2277 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى , قال : أخبرنا عبد الرزاق , قال : أخبرنا ابن جريج قال : حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر , عن أبي عمرو مولى عائشة أن عائشة كانت تقرأ : { يطوقونه } ... وأما قراءة من قرأ ذلك : { وعلى الذين يطوقونه } فقراءة لمصاحف أهل الإسلام خلاف .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for His saying: {And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person}, the recitation of all the Muslims is {wa-'ala alladhina yutiqunahu} and upon that is the script of their Mushafs... whereas Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it, according to what is narrated from him: "wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu"... 2277 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us... from Abu 'Amr the freedman of 'A'ishah that 'A'ishah used to recite: {yutawwaqunahu}... And as for the recitation of the one who recited that as {wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu}, it is a recitation that contradicts the Mushafs of the people of Islam.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وأما قراءة من قرأ ذلك : { وعلى الذين يطوقونه } فقراءة لمصاحف أهل الإسلام خلاف
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And as for the recitation of the one who recited that as {wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu}, it is a recitation that contradicts the Mushafs of the people of Islam.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال البخاري : حدثنا إسحاق ، أخبرنا روح ، حدثنا زكريا بن إسحاق ، حدثنا عمرو بن دينار ، عن عطاء ، سمع ابن عباس يقرأ : ( وعلى الذين يطوقونه فدية طعام مسكين ) قال ابن عباس : ليست بمنسوخة ، هو الشيخ الكبير والمرأة الكبيرة لا يستطيعان أن يصوما ، فليطعمان مكان كل يوم مسكينا .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Al-Bukhari recorded: Ishaq narrated to us, Rawh informed us, Zakariyya bin Ishaq narrated to us, 'Amr bin Dinar narrated to us, from 'Ata', who heard Ibn 'Abbas recite: (And for those who are burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person). Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is not abrogated; it refers to the old man and the old woman who are unable to fast, so they should feed one poor person for each day."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: سمع ابن عباس يقرأ : ( وعلى الذين يطوقونه فدية طعام مسكين )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: heard Ibn 'Abbas recite: (And for those who are burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person)

variants.short_title: 2:196 — 'Establish Hajj and Umrah to the House'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Establish... to the House' for 'Complete... for God' in 2:196
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:196, the Uthmanic text begins 'وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ' ('Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God.'). Both al-Tabari (2599–2601, 2622) and Ibn Kathir record via al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Alqamah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (and endorsed by Ibn Abbas and Ali) it read 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' ('Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'), which Kufan jurists cited to show that Umrah rites end at the Ka'bah.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God
variants.variant_target_english: Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذٗى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٞ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٖۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٞ كَامِلَةٞۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God. But if you are prevented, (make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its lawful place. Whoever of you is sick or has an injury to his head, (there is) a ransom of fasting or a freewill offering or a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever makes use of (the time from) the visitation until the pilgrimage, (let him make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Whoever cannot find (an offering), (let him perform) a fast of three days during the pilgrimage, and seven (days) when you return. That is ten (days) in all. That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God is harsh in retribution.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators view 'Establish... to the House' as an exegetical reading clarifying that the rites of Umrah are confined to the Sacred House (the Ka'bah and Safa-Marwah) rather than extending to Arafat.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple authentic Kufan chains showing that Alqamah and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i actively recited 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' as the text of the verse following Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 2599 - حدثني عبيد بن إسماعيل الهباري , قال : ثنا عبد الله بن نمير , عن الأعمش , عن إبراهيم , عن علقمة : { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله } قال : هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت } قال : لا تجاوزوا بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير , فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: {Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God}, he said: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}. He said: Do not pass beyond the House during the 'Umrah. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id bin Jubayr, and he said: Ibn 'Abbas also said thus.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت }
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال قتادة ، عن زرارة ، عن ابن عباس أنه قال : الحج عرفة ، والعمرة الطواف . وكذا روى الأعمش ، عن إبراهيم عن علقمة في قوله : ( وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله ) قال : هي [ في ] قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت " لا تجاوز بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير ، فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: "'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House, so that one does not exceed the area of the House during the 'Umrah'." Ibrahim then said, "I mentioned this statement to Sa'id bin Jubayr and he said, 'Ibn 'Abbas also said that.'"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Adds 'During the Pilgrimage Seasons' (2:198)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran says 'There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord.' Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr recited an extra phrase at the end: 'during the seasons of the Hajj pilgrimage.'
variants.title: Addition of 'Fi Mawasimi l-Hajj' in Q. 2:198 (Ibn Abbas & Ibn al-Zubayr)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1770, 2050, 2098, 4519), Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Abbas (as well as 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud) recited Q. 2:198 with the added prepositional phrase 'فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ' ('during the seasons of the pilgrimage'): 'لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ'. Ibn 'Abbas stated that the verse was revealed with these exact words when early Muslims hesitated to conduct trade at the seasonal markets of 'Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz during the Hajj.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord.
variants.variant_target_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ
variants.variant_target_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.variant_full_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars classify 'fi mawasimi l-hajj' as an explanatory gloss (qira'ah tafsiriyyah) specifying the time when seeking commercial bounty was questioned, or a phrase whose recitation was abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 2050 and 4519, Ibn 'Abbas explicitly states 'thus the verse was revealed' (fa-nazalat: 'fi mawasimi l-hajj') and continued reciting it that way after the Uthmanic standardization, as did Caliph 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr in Mecca.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمِجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ تَأَثَّمُوا فِيهِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were marketplaces in the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. When Islam came, Muslims felt that marketing there might be a sin. So, the Divine Inspiration came: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ تَأَثَّمُوا مِنَ التِّجَارَةِ فِيهَا، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets in the Pre-Islamic period. When the people embraced Islam they considered it a sin to trade there. So, the following Holy Verse came:-- 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا
hadiths.highlight_english: 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَتَأَثَّمُوا أَنْ يَتَّجِرُوا فِي الْمَوَاسِمِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Mijanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets during the Pre-islamic Period. They (i.e. Muslims) considered it a sin to trade there during the Hajj time (i.e. season), so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ
hadiths.highlight_english: so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt:
3768 - حدثت عن أبي هشام الرفاعي، قال: حدثنا وكيع، عن طلحة بن عمرو، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
3778 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى، قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا ابن عيينة، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد، قال: سمعت ابن الزبير يقرأ: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
3768 - It was narrated from Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, from Waki', from Talhah bin 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
3778 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us... from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr recite: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال وكيع : حدثنا طلحة بن عمرو الحضرمي ، عن عطاء ، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " . [ وقال عبد الرزاق : عن أبيه عيينة ، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد : سمعت ابن الزبير يقول : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " ] .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Waki' reported that Talhah bin 'Amr Al-Hadrami narrated from 'Ata' that Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj." 'Abdur-Razzaq reported from his father, from 'Uyaynah, from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid: I heard Ibn Az-Zubayr say: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."

variants.variant_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.variant_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمِجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ تَأَثَّمُوا فِيهِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were marketplaces in the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. When Islam came, Muslims felt that marketing there might be a sin. So, the Divine Inspiration came: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way

variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 2:213 jumps directly from 'The people were one community' to 'Then God raised up the prophets'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices supplied the missing link: 'then they differed'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:213 — Addition of 'Fa-Ikhtalafu' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:213, the verse begins 'The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), leaving unstated why prophets were sent if humanity was united. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via authentic chains from Ibn Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah that the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b explicitly included 'then they differed' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَاخْتَلَفُوا فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), and also note that Ubayy read 'and so that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection' near the end of the verse.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up
variants.variant_target_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فَبَعَثَ
variants.variant_target_english: The people were (once) one community, then they differed. Then God raised up
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and with them He sent down the Book with the truth to judge among the people concerning their differences. Only those who had been given it differed concerning it, after the clear signs had come to them, (because of) envy among themselves. And God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.
variants.variant_full_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
variants.variant_full_english: The people were (once) one community, then they differed. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and with them He sent down the Book with the truth to judge among the people concerning their differences. Only those who had been given it differed concerning it, after the clear signs had come to them, (because of) envy among themselves. And God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars explain that the Uthmanic text relies on rhetorical ellipsis (idmar) where 'then they differed' is understood from the later phrase 'to judge among the people concerning their differences', while treating the Companion wording as an explanatory gloss.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the authenticated report of Ibn Abbas (graded sahih by al-Hakim) appealing directly to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('fa-ikhtalafu') to supply the verb required by the narrative logic of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 4048 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار، قال: حدثنا أبو داود، قال: حدثنا همام بن منبه، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون، كلهم على شريعة من الحق، فاختلفوا، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين، قال: وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ". وهي في قراءة أبي بن كعب: ( وليكونوا شهداء على الناس ) يوم القيامة ( والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 4048 - Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us... from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners. He said: And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed." And it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: {(And so that they would be witnesses over the people)} on the Day of Resurrection {(And God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path)}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون ، كلهم على شريعة من الحق . فاختلفوا ، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا " . ورواه الحاكم في مستدركه ، من حديث بندار عن محمد بن بشار . ثم قال : صحيح ولم يخرجاه . وكذا روى أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب : أنه كان يقرؤها : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth. Then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners." He said: "And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'" Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak... and said: "It is Sahih, though they (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Similarly, Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi narrated from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "The people were one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'

variants.short_title: Who Knows the Ambiguous Verses in 3:7?
variants.plain_english_hook: Scholars debated for centuries where the sentence breaks in 3:7; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices worded the clause so that only God knows the ambiguous verses' interpretation.
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:7 — Syntactic Separation of 'Those Firm in Knowledge'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:7 (وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), exegetes and theologians were divided over whether 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge' is conjoined to 'God' (meaning scholars also know the interpretation of ambiguous verses) or begins a new sentence. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud's reading was 'Its interpretation is only with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say, We believe in it' (إِنْ تَأْوِيلُهُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), while Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge say' (وَيَقُولُ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ), both syntactically precluding conjunction with God.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: No one knows its interpretation except God.
variants.variant_target_english: Its interpretation is only with God.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: He (it is) who has sent down on you the Book, of which some verses are clearly composed – they are the mother of the Book – but others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts (there is) a turning aside, they follow the ambiguous part of it, seeking (to cause) trouble and seeking its interpretation. No one knows its interpretation except God. And (as for) the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord.’ Yet no one takes heed except those with understanding.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators cite the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b as explanatory recitations (qira'at tafsiriyya) proving that a mandatory pause (waqf) falls after the name of God in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explicitly rely on the non-Uthmanic wording of Ibn Mas'ud ('in ta'wiluhu illa 'inda Allah') and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('wa yaqulu al-rasikhuna') to settle a foundational theological dispute over whether human scholars can know the ta'wil of the mutashabihat.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وهو فيما بلغني مع ذلك في قراءة أبي : " ويقول الراسخون في العلم " كما ذكرناه عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤه ; وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And that is, along with that, according to what reached me regarding the recitation of Ubayy: "and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say", just as we mentioned it from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it; and in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say".
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وحكى ابن جرير أن في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إن تأويله إلا عند الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به " . وكذا عن أبي بن كعب . واختار ابن جرير هذا القول .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: "Its interpretation is only with Allah, and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it.'" And similarly it was narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b. Ibn Jarir preferred this opinion.

variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'what you enjoy from them, give them their marriage gifts,' Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas read 'what you enjoy from them for a specified term.'
variants.title: Addition of 'For a Specified Term' (Ilā Ajalin Musammā) in 4:24
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 4:24, the Uthmanic text reads 'فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ' ('So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b and the recitation of Ibn Abbas added the legal stipulation 'إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى' ('for a specified term'), with Ibn Abbas swearing three times that God revealed the verse with this phrase.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى
variants.variant_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way for a specified term
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
variants.variant_full_english: And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way for a specified term, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Sunni commentators argue that the phrase 'for a specified term' was either an explanatory gloss (qirā'a tafsīriyya) referring to early temporary marriage (mut'ah) or a wording whose recitation and legal ruling were subsequently abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tafsir al-Tabari (7181–7182), witnesses testify to physically inspecting the written Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b containing the phrase, and when Abu Nadrah objected that he did not read it that way, Ibn Abbas swore by God three times that God revealed it thus.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7181 - حدثنا أبو كريب , قال : ثنا يحيى بن عيسى , قال : ثنا نصير بن أبي الأشعث , قال : ثني حبيب بن أبي ثابت , عن أبيه , قال : أعطاني ابن عباس مصحفا , فقال : هذا على قراءة أبي . قال أبو كريب , قال يحيى : فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " . 7184 - حدثنا ابن بشار , قال : ثنا عبد الأعلى , قال : ثنا سعيد , عن قتادة , قال : في قراءة أبي بن كعب : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 7181 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin 'Isa narrated to us, he said: Nusayr bin Abi Al-Ash'ath narrated to us, he said: Habib bin Abi Thabit narrated to me, from his father, he said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a Mus-haf and said: This is according to the recitation of Ubayy. Abu Kurayb said, Yahya said: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term." 7184 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد روي عن ابن عباس وطائفة من الصحابة القول بإباحتها للضرورة ، وهو رواية عن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل ، رحمهم الله تعالى . وكان ابن عباس ، وأبي بن كعب ، وسعيد بن جبير ، والسدي يقرءون : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة " . وقال مجاهد : نزلت في نكاح المتعة ، ولكن الجمهور على خلاف ذلك ، والعمدة ما ثبت في الصحيحين ، عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب [ رضي الله عنه ] قال : نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نكاح المتعة وعن لحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر ولهذا الحديث ألفاظ مقررة هي في كتاب " الأحكام " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Companions the view that it was permitted out of necessity, and it is a narration from Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on them). Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and As-Suddi used to recite: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them *until a specified time*, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation." Mujahid stated that it was revealed about the Mut'ah marriage. But the majority are against that.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وكان ابن عباس ، وأبي بن كعب ، وسعيد بن جبير ، والسدي يقرءون : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and As-Suddi used to recite: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them *until a specified time*, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation."

variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran states that pagans call only upon 'females' (inathan) besides God; in Aisha's personal codex, the word was written 'idols' (awthanan).
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:117 — 'Awthanan' (Idols) in Aisha's Mushaf vs 'Inathan'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:117, polytheists are described as calling only upon 'females' (إِنَاثًا, referring to female-named deities such as al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat) instead of God. Al-Tabari records with a direct chain through Hisham bin 'Urwah from his father 'Urwah bin al-Zubayr that in the Mushaf of Aisha it was written 'They only call on idols instead of Him' (إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَوْثَانًا), and notes a related reading from Ibn Abbas ('uthunan', plural of wathan, idol).
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ إِنَٰثٗا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَٰنٗا مَّرِيدٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They only call on females instead of Him. They only call on a rebellious Satan.
variants.variant_full_arabic: إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَوۡثَٰنٗا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَٰنٗا مَّرِيدٗا
variants.variant_full_english: They only call on idols instead of Him. They only call on a rebellious Satan.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari maintains that the Uthmanic reading 'inathan' (females) must be followed due to the consensus of the regional Mushafs, explaining that the pagan Arabs gave their idols female names and called the angels daughters of God.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The transmission from 'Urwah bin al-Zubayr via his son Hisham is one of the most reliable family chains in early Islam, directly attesting a consonantal substitution ('awthanan' vs 'inathan') in Aisha's personal Mushaf.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10442- حدثنا سفيان قال، حدثنا أبو أسامة، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: كان في مصحف عائشة: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أَوْثَانًا ). قال أبو جعفر: روي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أُثُنًا ) بمعنى جمع "وثن".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10442 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: In the Mushaf of 'A'ishah it was (written): (They only call on idols instead of Him). Abu Ja'far said: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: (They only call on [uthunan] instead of Him), in the meaning of the plural of 'wathan' (idol).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كان في مصحف عائشة: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أَوْثَانًا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of 'A'ishah it was (written): (They only call on idols instead of Him).

variants.variant_arabic: إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَوۡثَٰنٗا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَٰنٗا مَّرِيدٗا
variants.variant_english: They only call on idols instead of Him. They only call on a rebellious Satan.
variants.hadith_arabic: 10442- حدثنا سفيان قال، حدثنا أبو أسامة، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: كان في مصحف عائشة: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أَوْثَانًا ). قال أبو جعفر: روي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أُثُنًا ) بمعنى جمع "وثن".
variants.hadith_english: 10442 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: In the Mushaf of 'A'ishah it was (written): (They only call on idols instead of Him). Abu Ja'far said: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: (They only call on [uthunan] instead of Him), in the meaning of the plural of 'wathan' (idol).

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Reads 'Their Chests Fold Up' in Q. 11:5
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'they fold their chests' (yathnuna sudurahum), Ibn Abbas recited 'their chests fold up' (tathnawni suduruhum), adding an extra consonant and changing the grammatical subject.
variants.title: Morphological Shift to 'Tathnawni Suduruhum' in Q. 11:5 (Recitation of Ibn Abbas)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4681 and 4682, Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Abbas recited Q. 11:5 as 'أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ' (*tathnawnī ṣudūruhum*, on the rare verbal pattern *taf'aw'il* with *ṣudūruhum* in the nominative case as the subject: 'their chests fold up / bend over') instead of the Uthmanic 'أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ' (*yathnūna ṣudūrahum*, with *ṣudūrahum* in the accusative as the object: 'they fold/cover their chests'). This variant alters both the consonantal skeleton (prefixing *tā'* and adding a final *yā'*) and the syntax of the clause.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Is it not a fact that they cover their hearts
variants.variant_target_english: Is it not a fact that their hearts fold up (tathnawni ṣudūruhum)
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ لِيَسۡتَخۡفُواْ مِنۡهُۚ أَلَا حِينَ يَسۡتَغۡشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Is it not a fact that they cover their hearts to hide from Him? Is it not (a fact) that (even) when they cover themselves with their clothing, He knows what they keep secret and what they speak aloud? Surely He knows what is in the hearts.
variants.variant_full_arabic: أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ لِيَسۡتَخۡفُواْ مِنۡهُۚ أَلَا حِينَ يَسۡتَغۡشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
variants.variant_full_english: Is it not a fact that their hearts fold up (tathnawni ṣudūruhum) to hide from Him? Is it not (a fact) that (even) when they cover themselves with their clothing, He knows what they keep secret and what they speak aloud? Surely He knows what is in the hearts.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 'tathnawni' is an intensive Arabic morphological pattern (taf'aw'il) close in meaning to the standard reading, though al-Tabari declares the Uthmanic reading 'yathnuna' obligatory due to the consensus of the garrison cities.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn 'Abbas's reading 'tathnawni suduruhum' is attested by multiple independent chains in Sahih al-Bukhari (4681, 4682) and Tafsir al-Tabari (17951–17954) and cannot be accommodated by the standard Uthmanic consonantal rasm ('يثنون').

hadiths.transmitted_by: Muhammad bin Abbad bin Ja'far from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ صَبَّاحٍ، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ قَالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ أَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}‏ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ أُنَاسٌ كَانُوا يَسْتَحْيُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّوْا فَيُفْضُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ، وَأَنْ يُجَامِعُوا نِسَاءَهُمْ فَيُفْضُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ، فَنَزَلَ ذَلِكَ فِيهِمْ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Muhammad bin `Abbas bin Ja`far:That he heard Ibn `Abbas reciting: "No doubt! They fold up their breasts." (11.5) and asked him about its explanation. He said, "Some people used to hide themselves while answering the call of nature in an open space lest they be exposed to the sky, and also when they had sexual relation with their wives in an open space lest they be exposed to the sky, so the above revelation was sent down regarding them
hadiths.highlight_arabic: سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: That he heard Ibn `Abbas reciting: "No doubt! They fold up their breasts." (11.5)

hadiths.transmitted_by: Muhammad bin Abbad bin Ja'far from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، أَخْبَرَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ، أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَرَأَ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}‏ قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا الْعَبَّاسِ مَا تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ قَالَ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يُجَامِعُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَيَسْتَحِي أَوْ يَتَخَلَّى فَيَسْتَحِي فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ‏}‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Muhammad bin `Abbas bin Ja`far:Ibn `Abbas recited. "No doubt! They fold up their breasts." I said, "O Abu `Abbas! What is meant by "They fold up their breasts?" He said, "A man used to feel shy on having sexual relation with his wife or on answering the call of nature (in an open space) so this Verse was revealed:-- "No doubt! They fold up their breasts
hadiths.highlight_arabic: أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَرَأَ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn `Abbas recited. "No doubt! They fold up their breasts."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ ذلك : ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ ) ، على مثال " تحلولي الثمرة "، " تفعوعل " ... قال أبو جعفر: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك عندنا ما عليه قراء الأمصار، وهو: ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ ) ، على مثال " يفعلون "، و " الصدور " نصب .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: {Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum} (Behold their breasts did fold up), on the pattern of "Tahlawli Al-Thamarah" (The fruit becomes sweet), "Taf'aw'il"... Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in that regard according to us is what the reciters in the cities agreed upon, and it is: {Ala innahum yathnuna sudurahum} on the pattern of "Yaf'alun" (they do), and "Al-Sudur" (hearts/chests) is accusative (Nasb).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ ذلك : ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: {Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum} (Behold their breasts did fold up)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ابن عباس : " ألا إنهم تثنوني صدورهم " ، برفع الصدور على الفاعلية ، وهو قريب المعنى .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn 'Abbas recited: "Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum" (Is it not a fact that their breasts fold up), with 'breasts' (suduruhum) in the nominative case as the subject, and it is close in meaning.
